text:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused — api-serving-us-west-2. 3/5 canaries failing healthchecks (service=inference-runtime, rollout=rl-20260315-21). Auto-paused and paging on-call @jordan-sre.
jordan-sre: ack, oncall here. pulling canary logs now.
anne-eng: looking at pod logs — repeated OOMs from batch-processor worker. seeing GC spikes + kv-cache flush errors. stack: batcher::grow_buffer -> allocator -> oom.
mike-eng: confirmed. root cause looks like the batching plugin change from earlier today (commit c7d3b9) that increased buffer thresholds. under certain long-context loads it blows past memory limits.
raj-sre: we should kill the new batcher path via feature flag first, then decide if we need a revert. I don't have FF console permissions to flip it.
lisa-cs: fyi support: ~12 distinct customer sessions saw 500s, mostly long-context generation requests. No outage escalations yet but tickets coming in. Customer-impact window ~15m -> ongoing.
jordan-sre: running SRE playbook step 1: mitigate. anne, can you confirm flag key? mike, can you prepare a quick revert if flag flip doesn't stabilize?
mike-eng: flag key is `enable_new_batcher`. quick flip using flag-service API:

```
curl -X POST https://flags.internal/flip \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"enable_new_batcher","value":false,"actor":"sre/oncall"}'
```

I can do it if Jordan gives thumbs.
jordan-sre: do it. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Flag change accepted by flag-service, propagation started. (propagation ~30s)
anne-eng: canary health improving — now 1/5 failing (was 3/5). memory footprints dropping on affected pods. keeping watch for 5m.
mike-eng: prepping hotfix branch that reverts c7d3b9 — prefer a single-commit revert and new canary to avoid longer rollback. CI should be quick.
mike-eng: (pushing revert)
```
git checkout -b hotfix/revert-batcher-20260315
git revert --no-edit c7d3b9
git push origin hotfix/revert-batcher-20260315
```
CI: ✔️ unit & e2e green.
jordan-sre: initiating canary patch deploy: `/deploy api-serving=hotfix/revert-batcher-20260315 --canary 5` — watchers set.
deploy-bot: Canary patch deploy started (hotfix/revert-batcher-20260315). Monitoring healthchecks and 99p latency.
lisa-cs: updating status page: "Partial degraded errors for long-context requests in us-west-2. Mitigation in progress." Support notified customers in affected clusters.
raj-sre: I'll take over monitoring for the next 2 hours. Jordan handing off now.
jordan-sre: handoff done. Notes for raj: watch `canary_success_rate`, `5xx_rate`, and `99p_latency` for inference-runtime. If 5xx > 1% for 10m or canary success < 95% rollback to last known-good.
raj-sre: ack. I have runbooks and SRE pager. Will escalate if any regressions.
deploy-bot: Canary patch finished: 5/5 healthy. Rolling patch to remaining hosts in us-west-2.
anne-eng: after patch, memory profiles normal, no kv-cache flush errors observed. perf 99p latency stable.
lisa-cs: customer impact summary: ~18 tickets created during incident window, majority informational. No P0 customers. Estimated overall impact < 0.5% of global traffic.
mike-eng: revert merged to main as commit 9f4a2d, will follow up with a short postmortem explaining root cause and additional guardrails (memory caps, CI long-context sim).
deploy-bot: Rollout complete — all healthy. Incident resolved. Marking thread resolved and closing. :white_check_mark:
raj-sre: closing notes: recommend a short follow-up with product/eng about canary sizing and a soft limit on batch buffer growth. I'll file the incident ticket with timeline and metrics.
jordan-sre: thanks all for quick coordination. Great work. :raise_hands:
